title: quant-kernel-packing-investigation-apr2026
collaborators: Kai Huang, Sofia Patel, Omar Reyes
content:
Summary: investigations into how data-layout packing and host-side copies affect end-to-end latency and throughput across quant formats (per-channel INT8, GPTQ, AWQ block quant, FP8 sim). This note focuses on the packing path (CPU vs GPU), interactions with fused KV cache, and concrete perf deltas observed on H100 and A100.

Test matrix: models and config
- Models: 6.7B small decoder, 12.8B medium decoder (same family as onboarding corpus).
- Hardware: H100 (PCIe) and A100 80GB. Single process, single GPU, single-stream concurrency unless called out.
- Quant formats: per-channel INT8 (calibrated), GPTQ-8 (posthoc), AWQ-block64 and AWQ-block256, FP8 (E4M3 simulated accumulation).
- Kernels: default matmul, matmul-int8-opt, awq-gemm, fused-kv (GPU fused layout), fallback matmul (generic).
- Workload: streaming generation average 40 tokens, tail up to 400. 200 sample prompts for quality checks.

Key findings (short)
1) Host packing (CPU) for fused-kv layout is the dominant tail-latency contributor when quant format and fused layout mismatch. On H100, memcpy+packing on host can consume 50-120ms per request on longer sequences.
2) Moving packing to GPU (simple CUDA kernel) reduced p95 by 18-25% in experiments and removed major CPU spikes.
3) Per-channel INT8 with matmul-int8-opt still gives the best latency/throughput on A100 for these models when packing costs are amortized.
4) GPTQ preserves quality best but incurred format-conversion overheads in our runtime; with GPU-side packing this overhead becomes small and GPTQ becomes competitive for latency.
5) AWQ block size choice matters: block64 had slightly better quality at cost of modest perf hit vs block256. AWQ kernels on H100 still need tuning for warp occupancy.

Detailed measurements (representative, 12.8B model)
- Float32 baseline (A100): median tokens/sec = 20 t/s, p95 = 360ms, model+kv = 38GB.
- INT8 per-channel + matmul-int8-opt + gpu-packing: median = 31 t/s (+55%), p95 = 240ms (-33%), memory = 24GB.
- INT8 per-channel + matmul-int8-opt + host-packing: median = 27 t/s (+35%), p95 = 285ms (-21%), memory = 24GB.
- GPTQ-8 + default kernels + gpu-packing: median = 29 t/s (+45%), p95 = 255ms (-29%), memory = 23GB, quality delta vs fp32 = ~0.6% average rouge drop.
- AWQ-block64 + awq-gemm + gpu-packing (A100): median = 28 t/s (+40%), p95 = 260ms (-28%), memory = 21GB; on H100 with current awq kernel: median = 22 t/s (+10%), p95 = 340ms (-6%), memory = 21GB (kernel fallback measured).
- FP8 simulated + fused-kv + gpu-packing: median = 23 t/s (+15%), p95 = 320ms (-11%), memory = 19GB.

Profiling notes
- Flame graphs show host packing appears as blocking memcpy in our traces; these correlate strongly with p95 spikes.
- GPU-side packing kernel design: use per-thread block fixed-size copy + small transpose for fused layout. This removed host memcpy from traces and enabled continuous GPU occupancy for GEMM kernels.
- Autotuner sampling still causes first-100-request variance on matmul-int8-opt. Bake map at onboarding.

Quality notes
- Per-channel INT8 calibrated: small quality changes, acceptable for most product routes after slight prompt tuning.
- GPTQ: best fidelity for instruction-following tests in our short set; rare failure modes exist around attention scale-sensitive prompts.
- AWQ block256: lowest memory and fastest packing but slightly worse ROUGE on some tests; recommend block64 for high-quality routes.
- FP8: promising for memory-limited environments but requires hardware FP8 native support for accumulators to be compelling.

Operational impact and cost
- CPU cycles for packing create higher tails under multi-tenant host scenarios. On our hosting footprint this translated into 8-15% lower effective throughput when host CPU was shared.
- GPU packing kernel increases GPU utilization slightly (couple percent) but recovers more tokens/sec net because it eliminates blocking host->device staging.
- For Dedicated customers with pinned nodes, shipping GPU-side packer as part of private deployment reduces variability and is recommended.

Actionable recommendations
- Short term (1-2 sprints): implement a GPU packing kernel for fused_kv layout and enable it behind a runtime flag; bake kernel map on onboarding to avoid autotuner warmup latency. Owner: Kai Huang.
- Mid term (quarter): tune awq-gemm kernel for H100 thread/block mapping and add adaptive block selection (choose block size at onboarding based on quality/latency tradeoff). Owner: Sofia Patel.
- Product: add a model onboarding report that explicitly lists packing cost (host vs gpu) and recommends quant+kernel pairing per route type. Owner: Omar Reyes.

Follow-ups for benchmarking and research
- Expand to 70B model classes and verify that GPU packing still recovers p95 when KV copy sizes grow.
- Add hallucination/faithfulness detector into quality harness; simple ROUGE not sufficient.
- Test with multi-stream concurrency and in Dedicated autoscaling scenarios.

Notes and caveats
- These results depend on current kernel implementations; vendor/kernel upgrades may change the sweet spot quickly. Keep the onboarding harness runnable and re-evaluate model profiles periodically.
- All numbers are single-run medians from a small sample; replicate on CI for final recommendations.

Raw trace excerpts (flattened)
- trace A1 (host-packing): CPU memcpy (120ms) -> course of blocking -> matmul idle waits -> gpu work resumes.
- trace B3 (gpu-packing): packing kernel (8ms) -> matmul-int8-opt continuous occupancy -> kv-fused latch small.
